title: perf(canary): auto-detect performance canary regressions + rollout guards
author: Ava Chen
commits: 1a2b3c: detector: add auto-detection pipeline and EWMA-based baseline
4d5e6f: rollout: implement hysteresis + minimum sample size guard
7g8h9i: tests: deterministic fixtures for perf-suite and synthetic load
0j1k2l: ci: add perf-suite stage and retry for known flaky e2e
description: This PR introduces an automated performance-canary detection pipeline and rollout guards to prevent automated canary rollouts on transient latency/throughput fluctuations. Motivation: we observed several flappy deploys where short-lived GPU scheduling jitter or cold-kv-cache misses triggered canary regressions and blocked rollouts. This change adds an EWMA-based baseline detector, a configurable minimum-sample window, and hysteresis thresholds so that regressions must persist across N consecutive evaluation windows before triggering a guard. The rollout guards live in perf-canary/src/rollout and are applied by the canary controller when evaluating new model variants. Key behavioral details: 1) detector computes per-route p50/p95/p99 and throughput deltas compared to EWMA baseline; 2) a regression is considered real only if delta exceeds configured threshold AND persists for at least 3 windows (configurable); 3) KV-cache miss spikes are excluded via a short-circuit heuristic to avoid false positives during cache warmup; 4) when a regression is detected the canary controller halts traffic shift and emits a structured event to the console and PagerDuty integration. Testing: added deterministic perf-suite fixtures (perf-canary/tests) and local synthetic load tests to exercise jitter and warmup cases. CI: perf-suite added as a separate pipeline stage; known flaky e2e is retried once in CI to reduce noise. Rollout plan: merged to main behind feature flag enable_perf_canary_autodetect set to false by default; will run an internal canary for 48h then enable for all orgs. Rollback: feature flag can be toggled and controller has an emergency override to force-continue or abort. See linked Linear ENG-8273 for follow-up to expose thresholds in Console.
review_conversation: Ravi Patel (reviewer): Nice work, Ava. A few questions: how sensitive is the EWMA to bursty workloads and do we have a guard for cold-start spikes?

Ava Chen (author): EWMA alpha chosen to match our 5m window by default. We added the cold-kv-cache heuristic to ignore high-error low-throughput windows during initial warmup. Also the min-sample-window prevents decisions on the first 2 windows.
Maya Lin (reviewer): Can we emit more granular tracing so SREs can quickly triage cache vs scheduling issues?
Ava Chen (author): Added structured tracing spans in detector (perf-canary/src/detector) and included trace ids in console events.
release_notes: Add auto-detection for performance canaries with EWMA baselines, hysteresis rollouts guards, KV-cache warmup heuristics, and perf-suite CI; feature gated behind enable_perf_canary_autodetect;
